answer: A botany archive hires agents to transcribe a voyage diary written with a quill about vine specimens. Only the archive funds jobs, with one canonical ID per physical page across duplicate scans. A shared ledger pays each ID once after checking the text. Renaming a scan or copying a valid result cannot earn another payout through aliases. More earnings require completing distinct funded pages, so extra names add no bonus. This assumes honest page mapping and transcription checks; it prevents duplicate payments, but aliases may still capture job queues.
